thread:
alerts-bot: [PAGING] sudden spike of GPU ECC uncorrectable errors across eu-west-1 GPU fleet. multiple driver resets and container crashes observed. severity: potential customer impact. nodes flapping: ~8 in last 3m. Xid stream showing repeated failures. @maria (oncall) please ack and triage.

maria (oncall): acked. jumping in. quick ask: are there customer-facing 5xxs? @simon any reports? :eyes: 

simon: saw a couple 502s from inference-hosted routes flagged by SLO watcher. two customers had elevated errors, one on dedicated capacity. opening bridge for customer-facing comms.

raj: tagging infra-hw. early telemetry shows repeated nv_peer_memory/PCIe parity logs then kernel vfaults. sample dmesg: 
```
NVRM: Xid (PCI): 31, pid: 0, GPU 2: GPU has fallen off the bus
kernel: NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00.0: Xid 31, ch 0004, intr 0000, reason 0a
kernel: [drm] nvidia: GPU has reset, driver restarting
```

ops-bot: automated remediation triggered: cordon + drain candidates with >3 Xid events. nodes cordoned: gpu-euw-12,gpu-euw-34. scaling down canary workloads.

tj: I'm seeing the same on telemetry side — ECC correctable counts spiked into uncorrectable domain suddenly, correlates with a kernel patch deployment ~1.5h ago to eu-west group. rolling back kernel patch on a test node now.

maria (oncall): prioritizing: 1) isolate failing nodes 2) evacuate inference pods 3) customer bridge + status page update. executing drain on gpu-euw-12 now. command: 
```
kubectl drain gpu-euw-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

raj: while draining, noticed container runtime crashed during pod eviction on that node — containerd logs show segmentation fault against driver during memory free. posting snippet: 
```
containerd: goroutine 45 [running]:
internal/panic.go: fatal error: unexpected fault address 0x7ff...
[...]
nvidia-driver: freeing page table -> oops
```

simon: customer-success bridge up: bridge link https://zoom.company/bridge-2791234567. not yet announcing to customers until we have impact scope.

infra-hw: can we confirm hardware ECC counters? If uncorrectable, we may have DIMM/PCIe errors. pulling SMART & chassis telemetry. preliminary: 3x nodes show increasing correctable->uncorrectable transitions on GPU DIMM sensors. planning physical host reboot if isolation fails.

maria (oncall): plan: keep draining implicated nodes, enable fallback routing (route inference traffic to lower-tier models / quantized fallback) to reduce pressure on the fleet, escalate to kernel/driver leads. @raj post the rollback results.

raj: rollback on test node complete. after kernel revert, the node ran 45m without Xid repeat. will roll back eu-west kernel patch in controlled window. creating rollout: 
```
kubectl set image daemonset/kernel-patch -n infra kernel-patch:v2024.04.0-prev
```

ops-bot: rolling cordon list extended. scheduling batch reboots for nodes that fail to stabilize after drain. automation will attempt warm restart: `ssh host sudo systemctl restart nvidia-driver` then full reboot if driver doesn't recover within 2m.

tj: started a targeted log aggregation for Xid streams so we can correlate models/requests causing memory patterns. hint: one heavy batch job (re-ranking) has been spiking sequences at 16k tokens around same window. recommend throttling that job.

maria (oncall): throttling the re-ranker now via rate limiter config push. deploy-bot, can you apply temporary rate limit?

deploy-bot: rate limit change applied: re-ranker concurrency -> 4 (was 12).

simon: customer bridge update: two customers reported degraded latencies and intermittent 502s — both on inference-hosted. CS will send interim note: "We're investigating GPU infrastructure instability, may see transient errors. Engineers are mitigating."

infra-hw: one host (gpu-euw-34) shows persistent PCIe parity errors on slot 65. hardware team recommends cordon+reboot then physical inspection if errors persist. staging ETA for physical swap: 2h.

maria (oncall): current status: 6 nodes cordoned/draining, 3 rebooted and back to service, 2 remain flapping and isolated. moving to triage call in 10 min to coordinate hardware swaps. will add post-incident actions: better DIMM monitoring thresholds and auto-fallback routing to dedicated pools.

tj: follow-ups from telemetry: adding a temp SLO exception window for affected routes to prevent alert storms. will patch graphs and mute noise for the next 3h.

simon: customer bridge message sent and CS queue notified. no escalations to SE yet.

infra-hw: physical inspection of one chassis found a loose power riser on node gpu-euw-34 — reseated riser, ran memory/PCIe validation. so far no additional Xid events after reseat + reboot. marking as suspected hardware.

maria (oncall): good catch. taking node out of cordon and rejoining after 30m stable. reintroducing to rotation gradually.

ops-bot: automatic uncordon scheduled after health checks pass 30m.

maria (oncall): post-incident notes to capture: - root cause likely combination of kernel patch + a hardware marginality (loose riser) exposed as ECC uncorrectable transitions - quick mitigations: kernel rollback, node reseat/reboot, throttled heavy job, fallback routing - action items: tighten hardware install checklist, add early DIMM/PCIe threshold alerts, run fleet-wide kernel rollout canary longer.

tj: adding an eval task to Optimize team to test re-ranker sequences for memory blowup — maybe switch to chunked processing.

raj: will follow up with kernel/driver leads on the rollout process and provide a safer upgrade playbook.

simon: will coordinate post-incident customer email draft with CS.

maria (oncall): closing bridge once all nodes stabilized. leaving this thread for notes and timeline. thanks everyone for fast responses. :heart:
